note: Recorded live Claude investigation. Replayed tool calls run against the current database; claims are re-verified on replay.

hypotheses_considered.why: SwiftShip-EU accounts for 0.6816 of the excess refunds (Q2). Its refund rate is high across every SKU it ships, not just HDPH-200 (Q7). That points to a problem with the partner, not with one product.
hypotheses_considered.hypothesis: Fulfillment partner SwiftShip-EU is causing the spike, probably through delivery failures.

hypotheses_considered.why: HDPH-200 accounts for 0.6544 of the excess, and its baseline refund rate was 0 (Q3). Only 6 of its 12 refunds came through SwiftShip-EU (Q7). DEFECTIVE is its most common refund reason at 6 (Q8).
hypotheses_considered.hypothesis: SKU HDPH-200 has a product defect that is causing refunds on its own, separate from the partner.

hypotheses_considered.why: EU (Q4) has almost the same capture volume as SwiftShip-EU (Q2), and electronics contains HDPH-200 (Q6). Both look like overlaps with the two causes above, but the data could not confirm this.
hypotheses_considered.hypothesis: The EU region or the electronics category is a separate cause.

hypotheses_considered.why: Web, mobile and marketplace are all elevated (Q5), so the excess is spread across channels rather than coming from one.
hypotheses_considered.hypothesis: One channel is driving the spike.

final.hypothesis: There appear to be two separate causes: a fulfillment problem at SwiftShip-EU, and a product-quality problem with SKU HDPH-200.
final.observed_anomaly: The refund rate was 21.51% in the current window (20 refunds on 93 captures), against a 3.43% baseline.
final.explanation: SwiftShip-EU's refund rate rose from 4.55% to 31.11% and accounts for 68.16% of the excess. Its high rate shows up across all the SKUs it ships, which suggests a partner problem rather than a product one. Separately, HDPH-200 went from a 0% baseline to 41.38%. Half of its refunds came through other partners, and DEFECTIVE is its most common refund reason, which suggests a product defect. The EU region and the electronics category look high mainly because they overlap with these two slices.
final.uncertainty: I didn't check how HDPH-200 refunds are spread across partners other than SwiftShip-EU, or the refund reasons for SwiftShip-EU's other SKUs. I also couldn't rule out EU region or electronics as independent causes, because their shares are above 0.25. Every channel's share is also above 0.25. Refund counts per dimension add up to 21 while the incident reports 20, so one capture may have more than one refund. The samples are small. I looked at no individual transactions or PayPal records.
